labels.tutorial.welcome.title: Welcome to {company}
labels.tutorial.welcome.body: You are the IT department. Tap anywhere to walk there. The lift is the only way between floors: walk up to it and it takes you where you tapped. It is reliable, but it has its own schedule and no sense of urgency.
labels.tutorial.go_to_it.title: Find your desk
labels.tutorial.go_to_it.body: Your IT office is on floor {it_floor}. When nothing needs fixing, wait there. Staff who see you wandering about decide you are slacking, and management hears about it. The office has several definitions of visible productivity.
labels.tutorial.first_ticket.title: Your first ticket
labels.tutorial.first_ticket.body: Something broke. The list on the right shows open tickets: tap one to walk to it, then stand still beside it while you fix it. Password resets can be done right here at the IT desk. The ticket is a request for help, not a suggestion to move the furniture.
labels.tutorial.capacity.title: Fixes take office time
labels.tutorial.capacity.body: Did you see the clock jump? Every fix uses office minutes (the 'fix 35m' on each ticket) and the clock races while you work. More tickets will arrive in a day than you can fix by hand. This is considered a staffing plan.
labels.tutorial.patch.title: Meet PATCH
labels.tutorial.patch.body: That is what PATCH is for. Tap AI next to a ticket and read the proposal card before approving. PATCH works instantly, but every action has a chance to backfire. The risk is shown as a range because PATCH is confident, not psychic.
labels.tutorial.automate.title: Automate the repeats
labels.tutorial.automate.body: When the same kind of ticket keeps coming, open PATCH and choose 'We keep getting the same tickets'. An automation runs every hour on its own, and each run is a fresh risk. Start small: one floor, staged. Repetition is useful; repeated mistakes are still repetition.
labels.tutorial.needs.title: Look after yourself
labels.tutorial.needs.body: Fixes and a growing backlog raise your Stress; Hunger makes it rise faster. Stressed, you fix more slowly, and at the top you snap at someone. Tap Eat (or a kitchen fridge) to eat; lunch is the cheapest time. A vending machine is not a balanced meal, but it is a recognised department.
labels.tutorial.end.title: Stay or go
labels.tutorial.end.body: At the end of each day you can carry on or hand in notice. Quitting is not failing: you keep every PATCH Point, PATCH keeps its upgrades, and the next job pays better. Good luck. You are allowed to leave before management writes a longer list.
